title: Isolation of F-specific Inovirus filamentous phages from environmental sewage samples
author: Theriault, Cook, et al.

steps.title: Prepare and enrich sewage filtrate
steps.instruction: Process raw sewage, inoculate with host, and enrich phage-containing supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge raw sewage at 5,000 × g for 30 min to pellet particulate matter.
Pass the supernatant through a 0.22 µm Whatman syringe filter and store the filtrate at 4 °C.
Inoculate a fresh overnight culture of E. coli K37:HFr (ATCC 33626) into a mixture of 5 mL 2× LB‑Lennox broth, 4 mM CaCl₂, and 5 mL of the filtered sewage filtrate.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 48 h while shaking at 50 rpm.
After incubation, centrifuge the culture at 5,000 × g for 30 min to pellet cells.
Filter the resulting supernatant through a 0.22 µm Whatman syringe filter and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Perform double agar overlay plating
steps.instruction: Plate serial dilutions of the enriched filtrate with log‑phase host to isolate plaques.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate a fresh overnight culture of E. coli K37:HFr (ATCC 33626) 1:100 into LB‑Lennox broth and grow at 37 °C, 150 rpm until OD₆₀₀ = 0.3–0.5 (early log phase).
Prepare ten‑fold serial dilutions of the enriched, filtered sewage preparation in SM buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.5; 100 mM NaCl; 8.1 mM MgSO₄) ranging from 10⁻⁴ to 10⁻⁸.
For each dilution, combine in a tube: 3 mL molten 0.4 % LB‑Lennox agar supplemented with 2 mM CaCl₂, 200 µL early‑log‑phase E. coli, and 100 µL of the dilution.
Pour the mixture evenly onto a bottom agar plate containing LB‑Lennox medium solidified with 1.5 % agar.
Incubate the overlay plates at 37 °C overnight to allow plaque formation.

steps.title: Purify filamentous plaques
steps.instruction: Isolate individual non‑lytic plaques and obtain clonal hazy plaques through repeated overlay plating.

substeps.instruction: Aseptically pick five individual non‑lytic, hazy, turbid plaques from the overlay plates and resuspend each in 50 µL sterile SM buffer.
Serially dilute each plaque suspension to 10⁻⁶ in SM buffer.
Plate each dilution using the double agar overlay method described above.
Repeat the plaque‑picking, dilution, and overlay plating cycle three times until each plate shows a uniform, clonal population of hazy plaques.
Store each isolated plaque at 4 °C in SM buffer.

steps.title: Confirm phage by PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify pVIII and pIII gene regions from plaque DNA and analyse by agarose gel electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: For each plaque pick, assemble a 25 µL PCR reaction containing: 5 µL plaque suspension in SM buffer, 12.5 µL GoTaq® Master Mix (Promega), 0.5 µL of 10 µM forward primer, 0.5 µL of 10 µM reverse primer (both targeting pVIII/pIII), and 6.5 µL nuclease‑free water.
Run PCR with an annealing temperature of 65 °C for 30 cycles (denaturation/extension steps per manufacturer’s protocol).
Include a positive control (M13 phage ATCC 15669‑B1 plaque pick) and two negative controls (E. coli K37:HFr in SM buffer and SM buffer alone).
Load PCR products onto a 2 % agarose gel and electrophorese at 90 V for 60 min.
Stain the gel with 1× GelRed® and visualise bands using an Axygen UV‑gel documentation system.

steps.title: Amplify phage and extract DNA
steps.instruction: Grow phage‑positive isolates, purify virions, and extract genomic DNA for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: In 20 mL LB‑Lennox broth, add 5 µL of each PCR‑positive plaque and 200 µL log‑phase E. coli K37:HFr; incubate 16 h at 37 °C with shaking at 100 rpm.
Centrifuge cultures at 3,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C and filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm Whatman syringe filter.
Concentrate the filtered supernatant using Amicon Ultra‑4 100 kDa centrifugal filters by centrifuging at 4,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C until the entire volume passes through.
Wash the filters twice with 10 mL SM buffer, then resuspend the retained phage in 1 mL sterile SM buffer and filter‑sterilise again through a 0.22 µm filter.
Treat 400 µL of each phage preparation with 10 µL DNAse I (2000 U/mL) and 10 µL RNAse If (50 000 U/mL); incubate 1 h at 37 °C.
Add 40 µL Proteinase K (800 U/mL) and 2 % SDS; incubate 56 °C for 1 h, then place on ice for 5 min.
Add 400 µL undiluted phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol, invert gently for 5 min at room temperature, and centrifuge at 13 000 × g for 5 min.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase (≈440 µL) to a clean tube, add 0.1 vol (44 µL) 3 M sodium acetate and 0.7 vol (308 µL) ice‑cold 100 % isopropanol; mix and incubate at –20 °C for 1 h.
Centrifuge at 17 900 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, wash the pellet with ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, and centrifuge again at 17 900 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the ethanol, air‑dry the DNA pellet for 20 min at room temperature, and resuspend in sterile nuclease‑free water.
Submit the purified DNA for Illumina short‑read sequencing.

steps.title: Assemble reads and BLAST analysis
steps.instruction: Assemble sequencing reads and verify phage identity by BLAST.

substeps.instruction: Upload the raw Illumina reads to the BV‑BRC online SPAdes genome assembler (v4.0.0) and run with minimum contig coverage set to 50.0 and minimum contig length set to 300 bp.
Perform nucleotide BLAST (NCBI Blast v2.16.0) on the assembled contigs to confirm identity to known F‑type filamentous phage genomes.
